pictures.scene: Coen Metzelaar, Aan de Oise - the quiet green river with the trees crowding the bank and the boat lying moored under its hanging canvas, by the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion, there on the willows we hung our harps
pictures.name: pd_metzelaar_wilgen

pictures.scene: Jan van Bijlert, De luitspeler - the young man in his broad hat singing with both hands on the strings of the lute, for there our captors requested a song, our tormentors demanded songs of joy
pictures.name: pd_bijlert_lied

pictures.scene: Hubert Robert, The Farandole Amidst Egyptian Monuments - the dancers going round hand in hand with the tambourine beside the broken obelisk under the pyramid, sing us a song of Zion they said, how can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land, if I forget you O Jerusalem may my right hand cease to function
pictures.name: pd_robert_vreemde

pictures.scene: Jan Adriaensz van Staveren, Een biddende kluizenaar in een ruine - the old hermit kneeling with his hands clasped over the great open book under the dead tree in the ruined arcade, may my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not exalt Jerusalem as my greatest joy, remember O LORD
pictures.name: pd_staveren_gedenk

pictures.scene: Paulus van Hillegaert, Prins Frederik Hendrik bij de belegering van s-Hertogenbosch - the commanders sitting their horses at the edge of the siege camp with the tents and the siegeworks spread over the plain towards the city, the sons of Edom on the day Jerusalem fell, destroy it they said, tear it down to its foundations
pictures.name: pd_hillegaert_fundamenten

pictures.scene: Nicolaes Berchem, Italiaanse ruine - the enormous ruined wall hung with ivy standing over the herders driving their cattle through the shallow water at its foot, O Daughter of Babylon doomed to destruction, blessed is he who repays you as you have done to us
pictures.name: pd_berchem_ondergang

lines.text: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept
when we remembered Zion.
There on the willows
we hung our harps,
for there our captors requested a song;
our tormentors demanded songs of joy:
“Sing us a song of Zion.”
How can we sing a song of the LORD
in a foreign land?
If I forget you, O Jerusalem,
may my right hand cease to function.
May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth
if I do not remember you,
if I do not exalt Jerusalem
as my greatest joy!
Remember, O LORD,
the sons of Edom on the day Jerusalem fell:
“Destroy it,” they said,
“tear it down to its foundations!”
O Daughter of Babylon,
doomed to destruction,
blessed is he who repays you
as you have done to us.
Blessed is he who seizes your infants
and dashes them against the rocks.
